comments.body:
CI fails here on `tests/test_validate.py::test_col_vals_not_in_set_nan`, an existing test that says "Polars treats it as a value" and expects NaN to pass `col_vals_not_in_set()` on Polars. So the current behavior looks intentional. This PR changes it to match pandas and the `MissingSpec` handling from #484, where NaN counts as missing.

Which behavior do you want for `col_vals_not_in_set()`? If Polars NaN should stay a value, this can be closed. If it should follow pandas, the existing test can be updated in this PR. #485 and #486 (`col_vals_between()` / `col_vals_outside()`) don't depend on this choice.
